entries.section: Section 7, Example 63 and paragraphs on root, third, fifth and the order of major/minor thirds
entries.evidence: Triads stack two thirds. Major uses 4 then 3 semitones; minor uses 3 then 4. A triad in root position consists of root, third and fifth.
entries.application: Independent check of A-C-E, C-E-G and C-Eb-G, with octave/register checked against MIDI. Also supports the distinct qualities of C–E and D–F in the new melodic interval lessons; these two-note exercises are not triads. Batch 08: section 7, paragraph following Example 63, explicitly names E–G and D–F as minor thirds (3 semitones); checked in registers E4/G4 and D3/F3. Batch 09: C4–E4 has 4 semitones (major third); E3–G3 has 3 (minor third), as explicitly named following Example 63.
